title: Officer's Actions Lead to Serious Backlash
description:
► Code Blue Cam Merch 
http://www.codebluecam.com/

Officer Matthew Knutson, a 13-year veteran with the Green Bay Police department, is accused of misconduct in public office and negligent operation of a vehicle. He allegedly used his squad car to intentionally strike a man who was fleeing from the police in November 2021. The criminal complaint points out disparities between Knutson's report and the released video footage, indicating potential inaccuracies in his account of the incident. As of June 15, 2023, Knutson's attorney filed a motion to dismiss the charges. 

The purpose of the featured content is to show the law enforcement interaction. It is NOT to publicly shame, ridicule, or degrade the individuals involved. Today’s world is swarmed with politics and conversations that are often misleading about our law enforcement officers. We feel it is vastly significant and imperative to show these interactions in their respective environments to inform and educate the overall public.

Almost 11 months later, the Brown County District Attorney's Office contacted the Green Bay Police Department regarding Officer Knutson's actions that night. The body cam and squad car video of the incident, were immediately reviewed alongside Officer Knutzen's police report. While examining the report, it revealed inconsistencies in his explanation of how his squad car came into contact with Robert during the pursuit. Following the assessment of the footage, Officer Knutzen was placed on paid administrative leave, and the Green Bay Police Chief requested an investigation to be conducted by the sheriff's office. Approximately six months passed, and the DA's office officially filed a criminal complaint against Officer Knutzen. The police chief made a public statement saying, we take all allegations of misconduct by Green Bay police officers seriously. I will not tolerate excessive force, ethical violations, or criminal activity by GbPD members. In Officer Knutzen's report, he stated, I started to pull my vehicle up on the western side of the driveway. In order to get my vehicle out of the roadway due to the other vehicles already on the road, the criminal complaint emphasized that statement. saying, you will find in his report that he describes him hitting Robert with his squad car at the last second and other vehicles being in the road. The squad camera tells a different story. There is no other vehicle in the roadway in front of Officer Knutzen's right to left and headed towards a driveway. The district attorney further explained, there was no need for Officer Knutzen to drive on the grass as there was no other vehicle in the driveway at that time. Additionally, he mentioned the officers on scene seemed to be amused by Robert's situation. He mentioned the timestamp of the occurrence, saying, After placing Robert in the rear of the squad car, Knutzen can be seen mimicking Robert hobbling after being struck to the laughter of the other officers on scene. It was also discovered that the use of force sheet submitted by Knudsen did not mention him striking Robert with his squad car. The district attorney said Knutzen gave a further indication that he meant to imply he had struck Robert accidentally. Without the use of force sheet, and some of the video recordings being disclosed, It is hard to determine how reliable these statements are. However, this wasn't the first time Officer Knutzen was investigated for his conduct. In 2018, Officer Knutzen was one of nine other officers that were suspended because of a harassment investigation. A report of the internal investigation stated there was a pattern of harassment by a small group of night shift officers. Some officers who were interviewed during the investigation described the night shift atmosphere like a frat house. The report further showed a female officer was the victim of hazing and harassment. She reportedly was so stressed out that she had to take off work to avoid harassment. Officer Matthew Knutzen, the 13-year veteran of the Green Bay Police Department, was charged with felony misconduct in public office, and misdemeanor negligent operation of a vehicle. Robert was charged with misdemeanor counts of resisting, obstructing an officer, and operating while revoked. On the prosecutor's motion, both charges were dismissed. shortly before the DA's office informed the police department of Officer Knutzen's conduct.
